title: GCONV_PATH can decide locale acceptance without loading executable modules
trigger:
VM fixture:

```text
gconv-alias/gconv-modules:
alias ASTRA_CUSTOM// ISO-8859-1//

latin/astra.ASTRA_CUSTOM -> astra
LC_ALL=astra.ASTRA_CUSTOM
LOCPATH=<latin>
GCONV_PATH=<gconv-alias>
```

No conversion module was supplied; this is an alias-only configuration.
measured:
- Reference `locale charmap`: `ISO-8859-1`.
- Real rsync with that GCONV_PATH: prints `ünï.txt` unchanged.
- Same real rsync without it: prints `\#303\#274n\#303\#257.txt`.
- Built helper with the shell's GCONV_PATH present in ChildEnv: `Loaded("ANSI_X3.4-1968")`, no warning.
closed_evidence: | Dropped GCONV_PATH | Closed for original case | Alias lookup and rsync evidence above |

title: deleted cwd plus `..` is not equivalent to its stale absolute pathname
trigger: VM: enter `.../deleted-with-parent`, remove it, and run the reference inheriting that directory. Pass that same now-vanished shell cwd string to the builtin helper.
measured:
| LOCPATH | Built helper | Reference locale from inherited deleted cwd |
|---|---|---|
| `../latin` | `Loaded("ANSI_X3.4-1968")` | `ISO-8859-1` |
| `../latin:<absolute utf8 dir>` | `Loaded("UTF-8")` | `ISO-8859-1` |
| `missing:<absolute latin dir>` | `Loaded("ISO-8859-1")` | `ISO-8859-1` |
how_found_quote: An already-entered but removed directory still has a kernel parent; resolving its vanished pathname does not.

title: truncated/malformed output and a reaping timeout can become a successful known charset
measured:
- 4 MiB stdout writer: killed after **5.004 s**, but result **`Loaded("X" repeated 1024 times)`**, no warning.
- Writes `UTF-8\n`, closes stdout, then sleeps: killed after **5.002 s**, but **`Loaded("UTF-8")`**, no warning.
- Writes `UTF-8\n`, keeps stdout open, then sleeps: **`Unasked("... did not answer within 5s")`** after 5.007 s. Merely closing stdout changes whether the same nonterminating child is reported.
- Invalid UTF-8 plus NUL: **`Loaded("�\0junk")`**; the exact charset consumer reports no warning.
- `warning: alien implementation\nUTF-8\n`: **`Loaded("warning: alien implementation")`**.
- Child writes a charset then dies by SIGKILL, or exits 7: accepted as Loaded without any failure information.
closed_evidence: | Output prefix/malformed data/nonzero exit/reap timeout accepted as success | Closed for original reproductions | All now Unasked; final blocking wait retries EINTR |
how_found_quote: VM private-namespace replacements measured: - 4 MiB stdout writer: killed after **5.004 s**

title: file actions can overwrite the answer pipe when standard descriptors are closed
trigger: If stdout and stderr are closed, `std::io::pipe` can allocate read fd 1 and write fd 2; addopen(2) then destroys the writer in the spawned child, and adddup2 copies `/dev/null` to stdout.
measured:
- fd 1/2 open: `CHARSET "ISO-8859-1"`, no warning.
- close fd 1/2 before lookup: `CHARSET ""`, warning `... /usr/bin/locale reported no codeset`.
closed_evidence: | Spawn fd 1/2 action clash | Closed | Both open-stdio and closed-stdout/stderr consumer runs report Latin-1, no warning |
how_found_quote: Same exact helper and charset policy on VM: ... close fd 1/2 before lookup: `CHARSET ""`

title: newlocale is not setlocale(LC_CTYPE, "") for composite names
how_found_quote: Evidence: `edges.py.log`; glibc `newlocale.c` explicitly parses a semicolon-separated composite.

title: documentation: narrow the new claims to what is established
trigger: A spawned executable **does inherit the signal mask** unless spawn attributes change it.
measured:
The fixture observed `SIGALRM_BLOCKED 1`.

Close-on-exec on these two pipe descriptors does not mean the child has only fd 0/1/2. A deliberately inheritable sentinel fd 3 remained open.

On this glibc 2.39 VM, ordinary failed locale loads produced a C codeset and **exit 0**, not the claimed exit 1 in `locale.rs:379`.
closed_evidence: The original five documentation findings are corrected in the new source/commit:

title: dropping every relative LOCPATH entry enables a different locale source

title: failed chdir does not prove the reference cannot resolve relative entries
trigger: There are three separately measured counterexamples to the inference used here:
measured:
| Context | LOCPATH | Helper | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cwd itself searchable, but an ancestor lacks search permission (`EACCES` when entered by pathname) | `locales` | ASCII | ISO-8859-1 |
| Same | `locales:<absolute UTF-8>` | UTF-8 | ISO-8859-1 |
| Deleted cwd; parent is still reachable in the kernel | `./../latin` | ASCII | ISO-8859-1 |
| Same | `././../latin` | ASCII | ISO-8859-1 |
| Same | `./../latin:<absolute UTF-8>` | UTF-8 | ISO-8859-1 |

title: a same-group descendant can still outlive the deadline
trigger:
VM fixture:

- Utility forks, writes `UTF-8\n`, exits 0.
- Descendant stays in the utility's process group, closes stdout and sleeps.
measured:
- Lookup returns **Loaded("UTF-8") in 0.003 s**.
- At **5.2 seconds**, descendant remains in state **S**, in the original group.
- Observer then kills and reaps that exact PID.
how_found_quote: `signal(SIGKILL, SIG_IGN)` failed with **EINVAL (22)**. A descendant that remained in the group while holding stdout was killed despite ignoring SIGTERM/SIGINT, reached **Z**, and was reaped by the observer with status 9.
